title: Man. Post. Cap. II §XIX: Garissoles — Tum in nomine imputationis; circumcision gloss charge
pass_a_gloss: GAR. Then in the name of the imputation of sin it is variously played. Section XIX. For at the beginning of the dispute we had agreed that by the voice of imputation in this business was to be understood either the act of a judge declaring someone guilty and worthy of punishment, or the infliction of the punishment itself. Now it is gone into all other things. For it is asked whether Adam's own actual sin is imputed to posterity. The Learned Men acknowledge it verbally; but hear the explanation: namely, they say, so that that transgression is said to be imputed in the same signification in which the Apostle said foreskin is imputed for circumcision, that is, to be held in the same place as if it had been circumcised: For we, on account of the sin inhering in us from the origin, are worthy to be held in that place as if we had committed the actual disobedience itself. Which someone might indeed not undeservedly claim ought to be reckoned to tergiversation. For it had been agreed that to impute sin in this place is nothing other than so to ascribe a sin to someone that on account of it, and by its consideration, he undergo guilt, and either pay punishments or at least be judged worthy of punishments. But how remote that is from that signification of imputation which they here propose, no one does not see.
pass_b_english: Garissoles: Next, people play various games with the very name of imputing sin (§ XIX). At the start of the dispute we had agreed that in this business 'imputation' means either a judge's act declaring someone guilty and worthy of punishment, or the infliction of the punishment itself. Now everything is shifted. The question is whether Adam's own actual sin is imputed to his posterity. The learned men grant it in words—but hear their gloss: that transgression is 'imputed,' they say, in the same sense in which the Apostle said foreskin is imputed for circumcision (Romans 2:26)—that is, counted as if circumcised. So we, because of the sin that inheres in us from birth, are worthy to be treated as if we ourselves had committed that actual disobedience. Someone might fairly call that tergiversation. We had agreed that to impute sin here is nothing but so to ascribe a sin to someone that, for its sake and in view of it, he comes under guilt and either suffers punishment or is at least judged worthy of it. How far their proposed sense is from that meaning, anyone can see.
source_text: GAR. Tum in nomine imputationis peccati varie luditur. § XIX. Nam disputationis initio consenseramus, per imputationis vocem in hoc negotio intelligendum, vel actum judicis declarantis aliquem reum poenaque dignum, vel ipsam poenae inflictionem. Nunc in alia omnia itur. Quaeritur enim, an ipsius Adae actuale peccatum posteris imputetur. Agnoscunt Viri Docti verbotenus; sed explicationem audi: ita scilicet, inquiunt, ut imputari dicatur illa transgressio eodem significatu, quo dixit Apostolus, praeputium imputari in circuncisionem, id est, eodem loco haberi ac si circumcisum esset: Nos enim, ob peccatum nobis ab origine inhaerens, dignos esse, qui eo loco habeamur, ac si actualem ipsam inobedientiam commisissemus. Quod aliquis sane haud immerito tergiversationi deputari debere pretenderit. Convenerat enim, imputare peccatum hoc loco non aliud esse, quam alicui peccatum ita adscribere, ut propter illud, & ejus consideratione reatum subeat, & vel poenas det, vel certe poenis dignus existimetur. At quam remotum sit illud ab eo imputationis significatu, quem hic proponunt, nemo non videt.

choices.choice: Keep Garissoles charge on name-play and agreed judge/punishment sense vs circumcision gloss
